This is the operational reference for agent roles: what exists *now*, where
each is defined, and when each fires. For the spec-level model (the four core
roles and install shapes) see [The four core roles](/internal/docs/spec/roles).

## The registry

**`AGENT_ROLES`** in `packages/agent-mcp/src/role-config.ts` is the single
runtime source of truth for built-in role ids — tool `roles:` allowlists,
quota keys, and `byRole` guidance all key off it. The set is open: plugins
contribute namespaced `<plugin>:<role>` ids at runtime.

The built-ins, grouped as the file orders them:

| Group | Roles |
|---|---|
| Pipeline | `scoper` · `architect` · `worker` · `validator` · `reviewer` · `debugger` · `documenter` · `curator` |
| Chat surfaces | `operator` · `oracle` |
| Pot | `cup` (the generic "do this task" agent — no pipeline spine, no chunk requirement) · `mug` (the Pot's placement decider — the `coding`/`work` Pot blueprint's `spine.decider`; steer-don't-dispatch placement) · `overwatch` (read-everything system-health supervisor; nudge/observe/escalate only — its role envelope **denies** `fs-write` + `bash`) · `planner` (interactive plan-authoring session) |
| Cross-cutting | `orchestrator` · `promote` · `security-reviewer` · `infra-reviewer` · `crosscheck` · `ui-qa` · `auditor` (read-only adversarial screen for remote-authored features) · `merge-resolver` (git-sync conflict resolution) · `content-fixer` (git-sync content-guard repairer — fixes quarantined files so they pass the content detector, leaves the tree clean, does **not** push) · `release-manager` (deploy go/no-go) · `release-fixer` (green-checkpoint gate fixer — reproduces a failing test, then fixes the code or quarantines a proven flake) · `papercup` (read-mostly fleet watcher) |

Two adjacent ids that are *not* agent roles: **`brain`**
(`BRAIN_PRINCIPAL_ROLE`) is an RBAC role on the operator's own *principal* —
"only the brain approves spawns" is enforced at the dispatch layer, never
carried by a spawned agent — and the per-feature **director** is a persona
(`blueprints/base/prompts/director.md`) that emits the decision verbs
(`NEXT_WORKER` / `NEXT_ARCHITECT` / `NEXT_VALIDATOR` / `DONE` / `ESCALATE`;
see [Decision telemetry](/internal/docs/harness/decisions-timeline)) rather
than an `AGENT_ROLES` entry. (The director is the **coding-factory** spine's
decider; the Pot's deciders are real `AGENT_ROLES` entries — `mug` for
placement automation, `operator` for decision-tree wakes.)

## Personas and layered resolution

Built-in personas live at
`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/base/prompts/<role>.md` — the
shared role library — with blueprint-specific overrides at
`blueprints/<blueprintId>/prompts/<role>.md`. (The old global harness
`prompts/` dir was deleted in blueprint-role-bundling; there is no
per-directory resolution `README` — the rules live in code, in
`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/prompt-resolve.ts`.) Resolution
walks the blueprint's **extends-chain** and returns the first match: the
blueprint's own dir → each `extends` ancestor → `blueprints/base/prompts` (the
universal library, always consulted). The old phase/department override axis
was deleted with it — `ctx.phase` / `ctx.dept` are no longer consulted. Where
a role splits a generic prefix from a blueprint specialization, the shared leaf
is named `<role>.base.md` (e.g. `validator.base.md`, `worker.base.md`), *not*
`base/<role>.md`.

Post-bundling, **`AGENT_ROLES` is the complete built-in role universe** — the
registry, not the filesystem, is the source of truth (blueprint-role-bundling
D-008). The const deliberately enumerates the blueprint-shipped specialist
roles too (`researcher`, `research-director`, `transformer`, `judge`,
`gym-director`, `migration-director`, …), so the persona file set and
`AGENT_ROLES` are intended to be co-extensive for built-ins. Only the
program-blueprint-scoped roles (`advocate` / `voter`, resolved via
`blueprints/vote`) and retired org-model roles (`ceo` / `coordinator`) remain
as bare strings. Chat roles (`operator`, `oracle`) are assembled differently —
by `packages/operator-core/lib/prompt-assembly.ts` from
`apps/operator/prompts/<role>.persona.md` + the generated tools catalog.

## When pipeline roles fire (the `coding-factory` blueprint)

The pipeline spine lives in the **`coding-factory`** blueprint
(`libs/papercusp/packages/harness/blueprints/coding-factory/blueprint.yaml`) —
*not* `coding`. (The 2026-06-18 rename moved the strict spine `coding` →
`coding-factory` and **reused** the `coding` id for the Pot blueprint:
`kind: pot`, `spine.decider: mug`, with only `DONE` / `ESCALATE` / `IDLE`
edges and no `scoper → … → curator` spine.) The `coding-factory` blueprint
declares the wiring:

- **Spine:** `scoper → architect → worker → validator → reviewer →
  documenter → curator` — each work item's kind/state determines the next
  role; the spine's `deriveNext` interpreter consumes the director's
  decision verbs.
- **Reactive overlay:** the `debugger` fires *before a worker retry* once a
  feature accrues `knobs.debuggerThreshold` failed attempts — read-only
  root-cause notes for the next worker.
- **Opt-in quality gates:** `tester` / `security` / `crosscheck` / `ui-qa`,
  e.g. `NEXT_CROSSCHECK` re-validates a pass with a different model.
- **Finalize recipe:** `onDone: [curator, postCuratorOutputs, documenter,
  archive]`; `onEscalate: [curator]` — the curator always runs on terminal
  outcomes (see [Why a curator](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator)).

Other blueprints are different shapes on the same engine — `blueprint:catalog`
lists what each one runs.

## How a role spawn happens

The DBOS pipeline (`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/`) dispatches each role
as a fresh one-shot agent process (see
[Why fresh contexts](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/fresh-contexts)).
The autonomous path and the interactive path are **two builders**, not one:
autonomous spawns go through `invoke.ts` (invoke-once), which keeps its own
richer inline assembly (substrate + feature-history + the G3 untrusted-peer
wrapping a headless run needs), while `buildRoleLaunchSpec`
(`packages/operator-core/lib/role-launch-spec.ts`) is the **interactive**
primitive that powers role sessions (`psu --role <role> [--feature F-NNN]`).
They converge on shared *leaves* — `resolvePromptFile` + `buildPrompt` over
the same role `.md` personas, the `session-launch-dirs` helper, and the
spawn-signing key — so the prompt is built identically and launch/resume can
never drift; what differs is the mode-specific context fed into that one
builder, and it should.

## Role disciplines that survive from the first generation

Verified in the current persona files:

- **Validator: default-reject.** "Your default is *reject*. The worker has to
  earn approval" (`blueprints/base/prompts/validator.md`).
- **Validator: run it or it didn't pass.** Evidence is enforced through the
  persona's test-gate Protocol — every test-requiring claim VAL needs a
  covering test that *passed*, an untested claim VAL is itself a `[FAIL]`, and
  black-box first: "Never read the worker's implementation code before running
  the tests." The rule that overrides any "looks reasonable" intuition is
  "Don't accept 'looks reasonable.' If you didn't run it, it didn't pass"
  (`blueprints/base/prompts/validator.md`).
- **Curator: sole memory compactor.** Only the curator deletes/compacts
  harness memory ([details](/internal/docs/harness/decisions/curator)).

The first-generation "role design rules" — one job per role, read-mostly
where possible, default-skeptical gates — are visible throughout the current
registry (the `auditor` and `papercup` are explicitly read-only/read-mostly
by design, per their `role-config.ts` entries).
